Convenience wrapper for marine heatwave event categories

Source: R/category3.R
category3.Rd

category3() is a convenience wrapper for adding or reading Hobday et al. (2018) categories (I Moderate, II Strong, III Severe, IV Extreme) for an event NetCDF file. New analyses should usually set category = TRUE in detect_event3 or detect3, which computes the same categories during event detection and avoids a second pass over the files.

Usage

category3(
  event_file,
  clim_file = NULL,
  hemisphere = "south",
  roundVal = 4L,
  S = NULL,
  sst_file = NULL,
  var_name = NULL
)

Arguments

event_file

Path to the event NetCDF file from detect_event3.

clim_file

Path to the climatology NetCDF from ts2clm3. Only required when the event file does not contain pre-computed categories.

hemisphere

Character. Either "south" (default, austral: DJF = Summer) or "north" (boreal: DJF = Winter).

roundVal

Decimal places for rounding. Default 4.

S

Deprecated. Use hemisphere instead.

sst_file

The SST used for detection (a file, a directory of daily files or a vector of files). Only required when the event file does not contain pre-computed categories.

var_name

Name of the SST variable in sst_file; auto-detected when NULL.

Value

A data.frame with columns: event_no, lon, lat, peak_date, category, intensity_max, duration, p_moderate, p_strong, p_severe, p_extreme (whole percentages), season.

Details

Categories follow heatwaveR::category(). For each event day the category limits are the threshold and thresh + k * diff (k = 1, 2, 3), with diff = thresh - seas and each limit rounded to roundVal decimals. p_moderate to p_extreme are the percentages of the event's duration (days, rounded to whole numbers) spent in each category, and the event's category is the highest one with a non-zero percentage. Works for both marine heatwaves and cold-spells (cold-spells are recognised, as in heatwaveR, by their negative intensities). The season is that of the event's peak month.

If the event file already contains categories, category3() reads those values directly, and clim_file and sst_file may be omitted. Otherwise both are required, because the percentages are counts of days, which need each event day's temperature.

Examples

# \donttest{
sst_file <- system.file("extdata/sst_test.nc", package = "heatwave3")
stem <- file.path(tempdir(), "demo")

detect3(sst_file, name = stem,
        climatologyPeriod = c("1982-01-01", "2011-12-31"))
